Organiser and coach Rakib Ahmed said a group of clerics visited the upazila nirbahi officer's (UNO) office this morning to demand the match be stopped. "The UNO suggested the two local sides settle the matter through discussion, and police later asked the organisers to postpone the match."

"We were forced to suspend it. Once the situation normalises, a decision will be made about holding the match later," he said.

Dirai UNO Sanjib Sarkar said permission had been granted five or six days earlier. He said a group of clerics later approached him expressing concern about possible disruption to local peace.

"I told the organisers, since both sides are local, to discuss the matter and reach a peaceful decision among themselves. The organisers then announced the suspension," he added.

The UNO also noted the organising club is not a registered body.

Mawlana Sharif Uddin, president of the Dirai Anti-Islamic Activities Resist Committee, said the objection was not to girls playing football – which had happened before without interference – but to what he described as the prospect of women dancing and indecency on the field.

"We are not against sports. We are against obscenity," he said.

Rakib Ahmed said the organisation has been holding girls' football events in the area since 2019 and local girls regularly participate in national-level tournaments.

When contacted, Dirai Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Aminul Islam said police had been prepared to provide security for the match.

However, the OC said, "The organisers themselves suspended it due to the situation that arose. The overall situation in the area is normal," he said.

title: Bangladesh must tap marine resources to achieve $1 trillion economy by 2034: Saki
lead: Bangladesh must make marine resource management a significant contributor to its gross domestic product (GDP) to achieve its target of becoming a trillion-dollar economy by 2034, State Minister for Planning Zonayed Abdur Rahim Saki said today (12 October).
clean_text:
Bangladesh must make marine resource management a significant contributor to its gross domestic product (GDP) to achieve its target of becoming a trillion-dollar economy by 2034, State Minister for Planning Zonayed Abdur Rahim Saki said today (12 October).

"Equal importance is being given to rail and inland waterways alongside road transport," he said at a seminar titled "Planning Perspective on the Emerging Industries in the Blue Economy Sector of Bangladesh".

The Centre for Bay of Bengal Studies of Independent University, Bangladesh (IUB), organised the seminar at its DMK Lecture Gallery in Dhaka.

Saki said the government had identified shipbuilding, port management and development as priority blue economy sectors, alongside improving connectivity between ports and industrial production centres.

The Prime Minister's Office has a dedicated Blue Economy Cell to improve coordination among institutions working in the sector, he said.

He stressed cooperation among the government, academia and the private sector to develop the blue economy and build a skilled workforce.

"Universities have a crucial role to play in developing the skilled human resources needed to achieve this goal," he said, thanking IUB and its Centre for Bay of Bengal Studies for drawing the government's attention to the issues.

Javed Hosein, a member of the IUB Board of Trustees, said inefficiencies in port operations and logistics were undermining Bangladesh's competitiveness in international trade.

Unloading a 21,000-tonne fuel oil tanker takes three to five days in Bangladesh, compared with four to five hours in Singapore, he said.

Garment exports also take around 95 days to reach their destinations after the fabric is made, compared with 60 days in Vietnam and 32 days in China. Hosein attributed the delays mainly to corruption.

Rear Admiral (retd) Md Khurshed Alam, director of IUB's Centre for Bay of Bengal Studies, delivered the keynote presentation on the prospects of the blue economy and emerging industries.

IUB Vice Chancellor Prof M Tamim delivered the welcome address, while Prof Bakhtiar Ahmed, dean of the university's School of Liberal Arts and Social Sciences, gave the vote of thanks. Marium Binte Hassan Farin, an IUB Environmental Science and Management student, moderated the seminar.

title: 8 platoons of Ansar deployed in Gopalganj ahead of AL programme on 19 Nov
lead: Eight platoons of Ansar and Village Defence Party (VDP) members have been deployed in Gopalganj to maintain law and order, protect public property and ensure public safety ahead of a programme announced by the activity-banned Awami League for 19 November.
clean_text:
Eight platoons of Ansar and Village Defence Party (VDP) members have been deployed in Gopalganj to maintain law and order, protect public property and ensure public safety ahead of a programme announced by the activity-banned Awami League for 19 November.

The deployment was made following instructions from the headquarters, according to a press release issued today (16 November).

The personnel will be assigned to key government installations, major roads and highways, and sensitive locations across the district, the release said.

It added that the deployed members were on high alert to protect important installations, prevent possible sabotage, arson and vandalism, and ensure uninterrupted public movement. They were also prepared to respond to any untoward incidents.

The release, signed by Md Nazmus Sakib, assistant director and public relations officer of the force, said Ansar personnel had earlier been deployed in Gazipur and Narayanganj to maintain law and order amid labour unrest and strengthen security in industrial areas.

Currently, six platoons are deployed in Gazipur and four in Narayanganj to secure important installations, industrial facilities and sensitive locations in the two areas.

The force expressed hope that the deployment in Gopalganj would help maintain stability and strengthen security across the district.

The government has held two high-level meetings over the past two days to review the security situation in Gopalganj following an armed march by leaders and activists of the AL, Prothom Alo reported today.

According to government sources, the government has decided to remain patient while keeping the situation under close surveillance. However, it will take a tough stance if the party attempts to create disorder or disrupt law and order.

The security measures come amid renewed AL mobilisation ahead of 17 November, marking one year since ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina was sentenced to death for crimes against humanity.

The party has also announced a five-day programme, including a nationwide lockdown on 19 November. Its activists recently staged marches in Gopalganj carrying locally made weapons, including oars, sticks and machetes, and vandalised police facilities and memorial structures.

title: Govt to meet Meta, Google to curb misleading content: Minister
lead: Science and Technology Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam today (4 August) said the government will engage with technology companies, including Meta and Google, to curb the spread of online misinformation, disinformation and other harmful content targeting the government.
clean_text:
Science and Technology Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam today (4 August) said the government will engage with technology companies, including Meta and Google, to curb the spread of online misinformation, disinformation and other harmful content targeting the government.

"Bullying, falsehoods and harassment on social media in the name of freedom of speech will be strictly controlled, and the government will not allow such activities to continue," he said while speaking as the chief guest at the inaugural ceremony of the Cyber Incident Reporting System (CIRS) at the BCC auditorium in Agargaon.

With the growing use of digital technology across banking, healthcare, education, e-commerce and government services, the risks of cyberattacks, data theft, ransomware, online fraud and identity theft have also increased, the minister said, adding that the newly launched CIRS will allow citizens and organisations alike to report cyber incidents easily and quickly.

He described the platform as more than just a complaint-receiving system, calling it an initiative to build trust between citizens and the state.

Mahbub Anam said the accompanying National Rating System (NRS) will help assess the cybersecurity capacity of public and private institutions, identify vulnerabilities, support development planning and ensure safer digital services.

Launched under the National Cyber Security Agency (NCSA), the CIRS is a centralised, web-based platform accessible at report.ncsa.gov.bd, where individuals, institutions and authorised users can report cyber incidents, according to officials at the launch event.

Citizens will be able to lodge complaints related to hacking or unauthorised access, cyber fraud, online harassment, rumours or disinformation, data leaks, online identity theft and harmful content, officials said.

Complainants can provide details of what happened, when it occurred and the extent of damage, along with screenshots, images, documents or links to relevant websites and social media accounts.

Once a complaint is submitted, the system will automatically generate a unique complaint ID, which complainants can use to track the progress of their case, including its verification status and resolution stage, officials said.

Under the process, a designated official at the upazila level will first verify the complaint and may seek additional information from the complainant if required. If the matter cannot be resolved at the upazila level, it will be sent to the district level, officials explained.

Complex cases or those of national significance will be forwarded directly to the National Cyber Security Agency for technical analysis and necessary action, following a process of reporting, verification, analysis, escalation, response, monitoring and resolution.

As planned, the National Security Intelligence (NSI), the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission (BTRC), and other law enforcement agencies will receive tiered access to view system summaries, statistics, and trends, which officials said would support integrated risk assessment, data-driven decision-making, and stronger national-level cybersecurity oversight.

title: Masked men ransack Hazaribagh courier warehouse in 18mins; 3 arrested
lead: Police have arrested three people over an attack on an AJR Courier Service warehouse in the capital's Hazaribagh, where at least 45 helmeted and masked men arrived on 23 motorbikes and ransacked the premises in just 18 minutes yesterday (21 October).
clean_text:
Police have arrested three people over an attack on an AJR Courier Service warehouse in the capital's Hazaribagh, where at least 45 helmeted and masked men arrived on 23 motorbikes and ransacked the premises in just 18 minutes yesterday (21 October).

Hazaribagh Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mosharraf Hossain confirmed the matter today (22 October), saying a case had been filed against 70-80 unidentified people in connection with the attack.

He also said the company filed the case last night.

Police later arrested three people in raids in Hazaribagh, he said, adding that investigators were reviewing CCTV footage and using technology to identify others involved.

Yesterday, the attack took place around 6:45pm at the warehouse on Mendi Dental Road, behind Shikder Medical College in Hazaribagh.

CCTV footage shows the masked men spent only 18 minutes at the warehouse, vandalising the premises and looting parcels, equipment and laptops.

According to company officials, the attackers vandalised the warehouse and office and looted customers' parcels, valuable equipment, office furniture and several laptops. They also allegedly took CCTV cameras and the digital video recorder (DVR) used to store surveillance footage.

AJR Courier officials said the attack stemmed from a dispute over land rent. They said the company rented the land from Sikder Group around two years ago under a contract and had been paying rent as agreed.

The company alleges that the attackers demanded future rent be paid to Sanzidul Islam Emon -- whom company officials described as a top criminal -- instead of Sikder Group, and threatened to shut down its operations if it refused.

However, The Business Standard could not verify these allegations independently.

Emon was not named in the case, police said.

According to the company officials, around 400 vehicles carry goods from the warehouse to different parts of the country every day. The attack disrupted transport and supply operations.

The case was filed by the company's human resources and administration department.

title: Forest-dependent communities stage boat protest in Sundarbans, demand crackdown on pirates
lead: Forest-dependent people and local leaders staged a demonstration in Satkhira today (9 November) demanding the elimination of pirate gangs operating in the Sundarbans and urging the formation of a task force to launch operations against them.
clean_text:
Forest-dependent people and local leaders staged a demonstration in Satkhira today (9 November) demanding the elimination of pirate gangs operating in the Sundarbans and urging the formation of a task force to launch operations against them.

They staged the demonstration in boats on the Kholpetua River in Gabura.

Protesters said forest-dependent communities have been left helpless, with most people unable to enter the forest to earn their livelihoods.

They alleged that they are being forced to pay extortion money ranging from Tk50,000 to Tk1 lakh to separate pirate groups.

They also called for the prime minister's intervention.

The protests began on 28 October, and have since spread across the wider coastal region. The Forest Pirate Eradication Committee has vowed to continue its movement until the Sundarbans is free of pirate groups.

Those who addressed the gathering included Moniruzzaman, joint convener of the Satkhira district BNP; Salauddin Liton, coordinator of the Forest Pirate Eradication Committee; and Solaiman Kabir, president of the Shyamnagar upazila BNP.

title: 14-year-old's body recovered after 3 days, 4 friends arrested in Ctg
lead: The body of a 14-year-old schoolboy was recovered from Patenga sea beach on Monday (17 August), three days after he went missing, while police arrested four of his classmates in a case over his disappearance.
clean_text:
The body of a 14-year-old schoolboy was recovered from Patenga sea beach on Monday (17 August), three days after he went missing, while police arrested four of his classmates in a case over his disappearance.

The boy, Mufid Ahmed Shawon, was a Class 9 student at Chattogram Modern School. Shawon lived with his family in the Chuna Factory area of Chattogram. Their ancestral home is in Sandwip.

Confirming the matter, Halishahar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Kazi Md Sultan Ahsan Uddin said all four accused had been arrested and later sent to jail through court.

"All four accused are juveniles," he added.

According to his family members, Shawon went missing on 15 August after handing in his answer script an hour into a two-hour exam, after which he went to Patenga sea beach with friends. He did not return home that day, and his mobile phone could not be reached after 3pm.

His family said someone demanded Tk1 lakh in ransom, claiming that Shawon had been abducted and was being held captive. The family sent Tk60,000 through bKash.

His father, Mahbubur Rahman, said Shawon would normally call if he was going to be late, but he received no call from his son that afternoon.

The family later contacted Shawon's friends and found inconsistencies in the information they gave. They filed a general diary with Halishahar Police Station that night.

Friends' account

During police questioning, the boys who were with Shawon told police that they had all gone into the sea. They said Shawon began to be swept away by the waves at one point and that they tried to hold on to him.

But they said they could not bring him back to the surface and eventually left the area.

The boys did not inform Shawon's family or police about the incident afterwards. The family also alleged that his schoolbag was thrown into the sea.

On Monday, Patenga police recovered the body of an unidentified boy from the beach. Shawon's family later identified the body at the Chattogram Medical College Hospital morgue.

The body was handed over to the family after an autopsy.

Family suspects foul play

Shawon's family does not believe the incident should simply be treated as a drowning.

They said the boys should have immediately informed the family or police if their account of Shawon being swept away was true. Their failure to do so, along with the alleged disposal of his schoolbag and the ransom demand, has deepened their suspicion.

Shawon's father called for a proper investigation and exemplary punishment for those responsible.

Police, however, said it cannot yet be determined whether Shawon's death was accidental or whether there was any other cause until the investigation is completed.

A case has been filed with Halishahar Police Station naming Shawon's four classmates as accused.

title: 11-party alliance alleges govt preparing to manipulate Thakurgaon-1 by-polls
lead: The government is preparing to manipulate the Thakurgaon-1 by-election in the same way as the 12 February election, Dr AHM Hamidur Rahman Azad, the assistant secretary general of Jamaat-e-Islami and coordinator of the 11-party alliance's liaison committee, has alleged.
clean_text:
The government is preparing to manipulate the Thakurgaon-1 by-election in the same way as the 12 February election, Dr AHM Hamidur Rahman Azad, the assistant secretary general of Jamaat-e-Islami and coordinator of the 11-party alliance's liaison committee, has alleged.

Briefing reporters after a meeting of the liaison committee today (23 October), he claimed a wave of public support had emerged for the alliance's candidate, Delawar Hossain, at Thakurgaon-2 and voters were preparing to cast their ballots.

"But I am getting information that preparations are underway to engineer the by-election on 29 October in the same way as on 12 February," he said.

The meeting was held at 11am at the official residence of the Leader of the Opposition and Jamaat chief Dr Shafiqur Rahman.

Hamidur said, "If the government does not want to remain in power, we cannot force it to stay. Its every action gives the impression that it wants to flee, making excuses to escape the situation."

Long march on 31 October

The Jamaat-led coalition will hold a long march from Dhaka towards Khulna and Kushtia on 31 October, demanding implementation of the people's verdict in the referendum, justice for the July massacre, resolution of electricity, fuel, gas, and fertiliser shortages, and measures to curb rising prices of essential commodities.

The alliance will also demand an end to corruption, extortion, and land grabbing, improvements in law and order, and an end to narrow partisan practices.

Hamidur said the long march would be peaceful, orderly, and people-friendly, with spontaneous public participation.

"We want the government to understand the people's concerns without delay," he said, urging law enforcement officials at headquarters and at district and upazila levels to ensure public safety.

The opening rally will be held at 7am at the south gate of Baitul Mukarram National Mosque in the capital. Jamaat Ameer Shafiqur will attend as the chief guest, alongside senior leaders of the 11 parties.

The long march will set off at 8am with a convoy of around 1,000 vehicles. The procession will travel along the Mawa road, cross the Padma Bridge, and pass through Shariatpur, Madaripur, Bhanga in Faridpur, Gopalganj, Fakirhat in Bagerhat, and the Rupsha Bridge before reaching Khulna.

From there, the convoy will proceed through Jashore and Jhenaidah before joining the concluding rally at Kushtia Zila School ground.

Media workers, doctors, artists, and members of various professional organisations will participate in the journey.

Six roadside rallies

The alliance has announced six roadside rallies along the route:

9am: Naodoba in Jajira, Shariatpur

11am: Kantakhali intersection in Fakirhat, Bagerhat

12:30pm: Babri Chattar in Khulna city

2pm: Swadhinata Chattar at Phultala bus stand

3:30pm: Murali intersection in Jashore

5pm: Bus terminal in Jhenaidah

The convoy is scheduled to join the concluding rally at Kushtia Zila School ground at 8:30pm.

title: Gazi Nazrul’s MP status in question after arrest; EC says parliament must act first
lead: The Election Commission (EC) has not received any official letter from the Parliament Secretariat regarding the membership of Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam, EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed said today.
clean_text:
The Election Commission (EC) has not received any official letter from the Parliament Secretariat regarding the membership of Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam, EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed said today.

“We have not received any letter yet from the honourable Speaker regarding honourable Member of Parliament Gazi Nazrul Islam,” Akhtar told reporters when asked about the lawmaker’s parliamentary membership following his arrest.

Asked what action the EC would take, Akhtar said, “We do not have anything at this moment. There is a legal provision for the Parliament Secretariat to inform us, and we must wait for the Speaker’s letter.”

Meanwhile, A Dhaka court today placed the MP on a four-day remand and his first wife Maksuda Begum on one day remand in a case filed over abetting the death of his second wife, Mariam Khatun.

Jamaat-e-Islami had earlier submitted a letter regarding its position, but clarified that official state procedures require direct correspondence from parliament, the EC official said.

The EC senior secretary added that matters concerning the status of a sitting MP after taking the oath fall strictly under the jurisdiction of the Parliament Secretariat.

Referring to newspaper reports about the lawmaker’s arrest and the required consent, Akhtar said the reports explicitly mentioned the consent of the Parliament Secretariat, indicating that the EC has no role or responsibility in that process.

Earlier in the day, EC Abdur Rahmanel Masud said that a criminal case or arrest alone does not automatically disqualify an individual from remaining an MP.

“Mere case or implication in a criminal case does not itself create disqualification for being a member in parliament,” he said when asked whether Gazi Nazrul’s parliamentary position would be revoked under the law.

Outlining the procedure, Masud said parliament must first officially notify the EC.

Once parliament writes to the EC, the commission will issue an official decision to clear any public ambiguity over the lawmaker’s status.

title: Armed forces officers given magistracy powers until June 30
lead: The government has granted special executive magistracy powers of commissioned officers in the army, navy and air force for nine days until June 30 from today.
clean_text:
The government has granted special executive magistracy powers of commissioned officers in the army, navy and air force for nine days until June 30 from today.

The Ministry of Public Administration issued a notification to this effect on Monday evening.

The notification said the order has been issued in the public interest and comes into effect immediately.

The powers will extend to three metropolitan areas and three districts where troops are set to be deployed during the founding anniversary of the Bangladesh Awami League, whose activities remain banned.

The officers will be able to exercise executive magistracy powers in Dhaka, Chattogram and Gazipur metropolitan areas, as well as Narayanganj, Gopalganj and Faridpur districts.

According to the notification, commissioned officers holding the rank of captain and above in the Bangladesh Armed Forces have been granted special executive magistrate powers across the country.

Army officers serving on deputation in the Coast Guard and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) have also been vested with the same authority.

The authority has been issued under different sections of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898.

Under the order, designated officers will be able to arrest offenders, disperse unlawful assemblies, conduct searches and take preventive measures to maintain public order.

title: Defacing Tagore graffiti: Bail denied to Ayas, Marzia after courtroom commotion
lead: A Dhaka court today sent Rashtra Sanglap Forum President ANM Ayas and his associate Marzia Khandaker Rimi to jail after rejecting their bail petition in a case filed over alleged criminal conspiracy, promoting enmity between classes and inciting religious hatred.
clean_text:
A Dhaka court today sent Rashtra Sanglap Forum President ANM Ayas and his associate Marzia Khandaker Rimi to jail after rejecting their bail petition in a case filed over alleged criminal conspiracy, promoting enmity between classes and inciting religious hatred.

Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Riad Hasan passed the order, Additional Public Prosecutor Muhammad Shamsud Doha Sumon said.

A commotion broke out between defence and state lawyers during the bail hearing, prompting the magistrate to leave the courtroom for his private chamber around 4:38pm. Several minutes later, he returned to the bench and passed the order after a brief hearing.

On October 11, police filed the case against Ayas and three associates, Marzia, Sakibul Hasan and Sujon Mia, with Shahbagh Police Station.

Later that day, Ayas and Marzia were placed on a three-day remand, while Sakibul and Sujon were remanded for two days.

On October 10, Ayas and the three others were detained over their alleged involvement in an attempt to deface graffiti depicting Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore on a wall opposite Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy in Segunbagicha, Dhaka.

The report said Ayas announced on October 9 that he would "erase" the graffiti.

"On October 10, Ayas and the other accused went to the spot. At that time, accused Marzia smeared black ink over the graffiti depicting Nobel laureate poet Rabindranath Tagore. She also attempted to spread religious hatred in connection with the upcoming Durga Puja, creating discord over religious sentiments and communal harmony," the investigating officer stated in the report.

On October 5, the DSCC had cleared the footpath in Segunbagicha of encroachments. Portraits of 10 prominent figures who made significant contributions to the country's art, literature and culture were subsequently painted on the adjacent wall.

The figures included Rabindranath Tagore, National Poet Kazi Nazrul Islam, artist Zainul Abedin and filmmaker Satyajit Ray.

title: Bangladeshi youth killed in BSF firing
lead: A Bangladeshi youth was shot dead by India’s Border Security Force (BSF) inside India, opposite Prithimpasha union in Kulaura upazila of Moulvibazar, early yesterday.
clean_text:
A Bangladeshi youth was shot dead by India’s Border Security Force (BSF) inside India, opposite Prithimpasha union in Kulaura upazila of Moulvibazar, early yesterday.

The deceased was identified as Tara Mia, 20, of the Murichhara slum area in Kulaura.

Lt Col Sarkar Asif Mahmud, commander of 46 BGB’s Srimangal Battalion, said the BSF opened fire on a group of alleged smugglers who had crossed into India’s Maguruli area through the Kulaura border around 4:00am.

Tara Mia was shot dead in the incident, he said.

The BGB official said a smuggling case had been filed against Tara Mia.

He said the BGB was working to contact the authorities concerned to gather more details about the incident and collect necessary information.

title: HC gives ACC 30 days to decide on probe into Shawkat Ali’s alleged $25m laundering
lead: The High Court today directed the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) to decide within 30 days on an application seeking an investigation into allegations that former Eastern Bank chairman Shawkat Ali Chowdhury laundered $25 million from the UK to the UAE.
clean_text:
The High Court today directed the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) to decide within 30 days on an application seeking an investigation into allegations that former Eastern Bank chairman Shawkat Ali Chowdhury laundered $25 million from the UK to the UAE.

The court also issued a rule asking the ACC and Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) to explain why they should not be directed to take legal measures based on information reportedly provided by the UK's National Crime Agency (NCA) concerning undisclosed overseas funds belonging to Shawkat Ali Chowdhury.

HC bench of Justice Fahmida Quader and Justice Md Hamidur Rahman passed the order and issued the rule following a writ petition filed by Supreme Court lawyer AHM Rezawanul Sayed, seeking necessary directives.

Barrister HM Shanjid Siddique, a lawyer for the writ petitioner, told The Daily Star that while investigating assets allegedly siphoned off by former land minister Saifuzzaman Chowdhury, the UK's NCA had reportedly found $25 million held in the name of Shawkat Ali Chowdhury.

"No satisfactory explanation" was provided to the NCA regarding the legitimate source of the funds, he said.

The writ petitioner submitted separate applications to the ACC and BFIU on August 12 and 13, respectively, requesting investigations into the allegations, but neither authority responded, Shanjid Siddique added.

Senior lawyers Mohammad Ali and Syed Mamun Mahbub, and lawyer Shanjid Siddique, appeared for the writ petitioner during the hearing.

title: PM for unified training system to make youth suitable for global job market
lead: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman today stressed introducing a unified, international-standard training and certification system to enhance the acceptance and recognition of the country's youth in national and international job markets.
clean_text:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman today stressed introducing a unified, international-standard training and certification system to enhance the acceptance and recognition of the country's youth in national and international job markets.

"If a unified and internationally standard training and certification system is introduced, it will not only enhance the skills of our youth but also increase their acceptance and recognition in the national and international job markets," he said.

The prime minister gave the directives while chairing the third meeting of the Governing Body of the National Skills Development Authority (NSDA) at his office in Tejgaon, said his Assistant Press Secretary K M Nazmul Haque.

Tarique Rahman said the NSDA is playing an important role in developing skilled human resources based on the demands of national and international job markets.

"It is also an important platform for increasing demand for Bangladesh's skilled workforce in the international job market," he said.

Stating that youth's skill development is extremely crucial, the PM said, "Although many training programmes are being conducted under different ministries to this end, these training programmes and certificates are often failing to play an effective role due to a lack of proper coordination."

"As a result, our younger generation is not receiving the desired recognition at the national and international levels against these certificates," he added.

The prime minister directed the NSDA Governing Body to formulate the necessary policies through a small committee within a short time and bring the skills development and training programmes of different ministries under a coordinated framework.

He also stressed introducing a system of providing training and certificates under a common syllabus.

The meeting was briefed on the administrative structure, manpower and functions of the NSDA.

Discussions also took place on the National Skills Development-related policy and strategy papers, development of skilled human resources in line with the demands of national and international job markets, sector-wise analysis of skills demand, and short-, medium- and long-term action plans.

The meeting also discussed improvement of training quality, certification and mutual recognition of certificates.

Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, PM's Adviser for Public Administration Md Ismail Zabihullah, Industries Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon, Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Minister and Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury, and Prime Minister's Adviser and PMO Spokesperson Mahdi Amin attended the meeting.

State Minister for Public Administration Md Abdul Bari, State Minister for Youth and Sports Md Aminul Haque, PM's Principal Secretary ABM Abdus Sattar, Executive Chairman of Bangladesh Investment Development Authority Chowdhury Ashik Chowdhury, Principal Coordinator for SDGs Prof SM Abdul Awal, Executive Chairman of NSDA Nazneen Kawshar Chowdhury, secretaries of different ministries and other senior officials were present, among others.

title: Allegations of hurting religious sentiments: Man dies after being beaten twice by mob in Satkhira
lead: A 30-year-old man died after being beaten by a mob in Debhata upazila of Satkhira on Tuesday night over allegations that he had hurt religious sentiments by making remarks considered disrespectful to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), police said on Wednesday.
clean_text:
A 30-year-old man died after being beaten by a mob in Debhata upazila of Satkhira on Tuesday night over allegations that he had hurt religious sentiments by making remarks considered disrespectful to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), police said on Wednesday.

The deceased was identified as Wahiduzzaman Shamim, son of Shamsur Rahman of Chhota Shanta village in the upazila.

Debhata Police Station Officer-in-Charge HM Shaheen said an audio clip purportedly containing Shamim’s remarks went viral on social media on Tuesday morning.

That evening, a group of people began beating Shamim in the Sakhipur area of the upazila. On information, police rescued Shamim and took him to Debhata Upazila Health Complex.

Around 9:00pm, a group of people under the banner of “Tawhidi Janata” entered the hospital and beat Shamim again, the OC said. As his condition deteriorated, he was referred to Satkhira Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead around 1:00am today.

Speaking to reporters, Shamim’s elder brother, Abdul Jalil, said Shamim had earned a master’s degree from Jagannath University.

Jalil claimed that about a year ago, Shamim fell victim to a gang that allegedly drugged and robbed him, locally known as an “ogyan party”, while he was returning home from Dhaka. Since then, Shamim’s behaviour had changed noticeably, he said.

He also said that on Tuesday evening, Shamim had attempted to take his own life by ingesting poison at home and had appeared distressed amid threats from people following the circulation of the audio clips.

Later, as family members were taking him to a local doctor for treatment, a group of people began beating him in the Sakhipur area on the way to the doctor, Jalil said. He added that Shamim was attacked again at the upazila health complex.

Arif Billah, an emergency department physician at Sakhipur Health Complex, said Shamim had multiple severe injuries. When his condition suddenly deteriorated, he was referred to Satkhira Medical College Hospital.

OC Shaheen said Shamim’s body was sent to Satkhira Sadar Hospital this morning for an autopsy.

He added that the victim’s family had not filed a complaint with the police station.

“Legal action will be taken if a complaint is filed,” he said.

title: Bangladesh launches first grid-connected agrivoltaics pilot
lead: Bangladesh has launched its first scientifically designed agrivoltaics pilot project in Chuadanga to promote renewable energy without sacrificing valuable farmland.
clean_text:
Bangladesh has launched its first scientifically designed agrivoltaics pilot project in Chuadanga to promote renewable energy without sacrificing valuable farmland.

Co-funded by the European Union (EU) and the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by GIZ Bangladesh in partnership with the Power Division, the initiative integrates solar power generation with the cultivation of crops such as green chillies and rice.

The Fraunhofer Institute is providing technical expertise to help develop the facility as a model for sustainable land use and local capacity building.

The project aims to create a scalable framework to help Bangladesh achieve its clean energy targets.

Data gathered from the site will help shape national policies aimed at balancing food security with the transition to a green economy.

The 49.6 kWp initiative is being piloted under the Green Energy Transition – Policy Advisory Partnership (GET-PAP) project, according to a press release.

Green chillies are currently being cultivated at the pilot site, while other suitable seasonal vegetables and rice are planned for cultivation in the coming season.

Fraunhofer ISE, a leading European research and development institute for solar energy, has more than 30 years of experience in the sector and is providing technical support for the development of agrivoltaics in Bangladesh.

Ahead of the official inauguration, hands-on training sessions were organised for local farmers, teachers and researchers, as well as officials from engineering, procurement and construction firms and system operators.

The capacity-building sessions focused on shade-tolerant agronomic practices, system maintenance and digital data collection. They are intended to equip local agricultural communities and industry stakeholders with the practical skills needed to operate, maintain and replicate the agrivoltaics model across the country based on scientific data.

Muhammad Khalequzzaman, joint secretary of the Efficiency and Conservation Division of the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources, said Bangladesh would be able to contribute to achieving its sustainable energy goals without compromising agricultural productivity and food security.

Ulrich Kleppmann, head of development cooperation at the Embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany in Dhaka, and Tanzina Dilshad, programme manager for energy, environment and green inclusive development at the Delegation of the European Union to Bangladesh, also spoke at the event.

As Bangladesh targets generating 20 percent of its electricity from clean energy sources by 2030, scientific data, crop-yield metrics and operational insights gathered from the Chuadanga demonstration site will help inform national policy frameworks.

The GET-PAP project is part of the Team Europe Initiative in Bangladesh, which pools more than €3.7 billion from the European Union, its member states and financial partners to help the country build a green and resilient economy.

In November 2025, the project also helped form a National Working Group on Agrivoltaics and Floating Solar, marking a step towards promoting renewable energy solutions that maximise the use of limited land resources.

title: Nvidia shares slide as chip giant probes CEO over spy claims
lead: Nvidia shares fell sharply on Monday after an internal investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort put his future at the AI chipmaker under scrutiny.
clean_text:
Nvidia shares fell sharply on Monday after an internal investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort put his future at the AI chipmaker under scrutiny.

The internal probe followed a media report that Huang had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who allegedly passed information to Beijing. Huang told Nvidia’s employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the relationship.

The investigation, announced on Sunday, has put a spotlight on Huang’s future given Nvidia’s status as the world’s most valuable chipmaker and the CEO’s role as the most prolific salesman of the AI boom.

The leather-jacketed Huang enjoys rock-star status worldwide, particularly in Asia, where he often mingles freely with fans, taking selfies and signing autographs for his devoted followers.

The fallout from the probe extended to South Korea, where Madison Huang, Huang’s daughter and an Nvidia executive, cancelled a planned visit to Seoul for an Nvidia conference that was set to begin on Monday, according to companies she had been scheduled to meet.

Nvidia’s shares tumbled more than 6 percent in Frankfurt trading, extending last week’s selloff and pushing the stock to fresh multi-month lows. At those levels, the chipmaker stood to lose about $270 billion from its closing price on Friday, according to LSEG Datastream.

“The market’s probably telling you now this does no favours to the stock whatsoever in a time when there’s a lot of conjecture as to the build-out of data centres,” said Chris Weston, head of research at brokerage Pepperstone in Melbourne. But Weston said he did not think Huang, whom he described as the “godfather of AI”, would be replaced.

“If we genuinely thought he was going to step down ... the stock would be down — it would be an absolute bloodbath, to be honest,” he said.

The New York Times reported last month that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, an unrelated former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, who US authorities investigated and concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset.

“The so-called Chinese spy narrative is purely a groundless accusation, slander, and a smear,” Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters in Beijing.

Megaspeed did not respond immediately to a request for comment on Monday, a public holiday in Singapore.

Alice Huang did not respond to the New York Times last month when it first reported her relationship with Huang, and Reuters could not determine her location to seek comment on Monday.

Shares in Nvidia’s key Asian chip suppliers TSMC, Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix rebounded on Monday after last week’s selloff of AI-related stocks. TSMC shares jumped 6.5 percent, while those in Samsung and SK Hynix climbed 2.9 percent and 4.7 percent, respectively.

Some prominent figures weighed in on Huang’s admission. Billionaire investor Bill Ackman, founder of Pershing Square Capital Management, said on X that the Nvidia CEO was an “incredible human,” but if “indeed this is more than an affair, then it is obviously a real problem.”

“I am hoping for a simple affair, not a risk to our national security,” he added.

Tesla CEO Elon Musk commented, “I agree”, on a post by Sequoia partner Shaun Maguire that said Huang “did something incredibly dumb” that was “bad for America” but that “Jensen is irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership”.

US President Donald Trump said on Sunday he had not spoken to Huang about the allegations, but called him a fine person.

“I hope everything’s fine. He’s done such an incredible job,” he added.

When asked if he believed he should have acted on intelligence when he was briefed about it, Trump said: “No, I don’t think so. I think he’s an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it. You have to hear it.”

The New York Times reported that Trump was briefed about the intelligence findings roughly a year ago and chose not to do anything with the information.

Madison Huang had initially planned to visit South Korean AI startup Rebellions and hold a question-and-answer session with Kakao Mobility. Rebellions said the events were cancelled due to “unavoidable internal circumstances at Nvidia.”

Nvidia AI Day Seoul, a two-day event expected to draw about 2,000 participants to discuss physical AI, agentic AI and infrastructure, will proceed as planned, according to South Korean media.

Nvidia did not respond immediately to a request for comment.

Analysts said a prolonged investigation or internal review could potentially delay Nvidia’s investment decisions or product launches, with broader implications for the semiconductor industry.

Ryu Young-ho, a senior analyst at NH Investment & Securities, said Nvidia’s rivals, including Advanced Micro Devices, could attract greater attention in the short term, potentially putting Samsung, which has close business ties with AMD, in the spotlight.

Still, he said Nvidia’s products would be difficult to replace, limiting the potential impact, although shipments to China could face further delays depending on how the situation developed.

South Korea’s deputy science minister said on Monday the government expected no disruptions to contracted deliveries of Nvidia graphics processing units despite issues currently facing the company.

title: Building smart cities in Bangladesh: The legal and regulatory imperative
lead: Around 60 percent of the world’s total population is expected to live in megacities by 2030, according to the World Urbanization Prospects 2025 report published by the UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA).
clean_text:
Around 60 percent of the world’s total population is expected to live in megacities by 2030, according to the World Urbanization Prospects 2025 report published by the UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA).

Dhaka ranks second after Jakarta, with 37 million people. The future quality of life of this population will depend on the decisions policymakers make today.

With emerging technologies, more countries are embracing smart cities, smart governments and smart economies to drive economic growth. Bangladesh’s progress in digitalisation positions it to set up smart cities with more efficient, transparent, accountable, responsive and citizen-centric administration and services.

Smart systems use information and communication technology and data analytics to improve decision-making, operational efficiency, government services and citizen welfare. Governments worldwide are adopting smart city initiatives that leverage digital technologies and data-driven platforms to enhance public services, promote inclusive growth, bridge the digital divide, and build sustainable, resilient and citizen-centric urban communities.

In a smart city, infrastructure and public and private spaces are interconnected through the internet and Internet of Things (IoT) devices equipped with sensors, GPS and cameras to collect data on public services, traffic, weather, pollution, noise, utilities and facial expressions. Data collected by smart devices is analysed, enabling informed decision-making, the design of innovative and cost-effective services, and savings in time and resources. Smart cities promote citizen participation, transparency, accountability, collaboration, social inclusion and problem-solving, which ultimately improve the quality of life and foster economic growth.

Bangladesh’s digital transformation has laid a strong foundation for improving public services and citizens’ quality of life. Consequently, emerging demands for efficient infrastructure and sustainable urban and rural development require the government to embrace technology, data-driven governance and intelligent solutions to ensure efficient, transparent, accountable and future-ready public administration.

Successful implementation of smart city initiatives in Bangladesh would require the coordinated deployment of technologies such as IoT, artificial intelligence, cloud computing, big data analytics and intelligent communication systems. These technologies can transform urban service planning and delivery across sectors, including transport, energy, healthcare, environmental protection, public safety and municipal administration.

By adopting data-driven governance and intelligent infrastructure, decision-making, resource allocation, service delivery, transparency, accountability and citizen participation can be improved. This would ultimately enhance urban quality of life, promote sustainable economic development and strengthen the competitiveness of Bangladeshi cities.

Despite these opportunities, smart city initiatives present significant legal, regulatory, institutional and governance challenges that must be addressed before implementation. The use of artificial intelligence (AI), IoT, data collection and automated decision-making would raise complex issues concerning data governance, privacy, cybersecurity, interoperability, public procurement, liability, algorithmic accountability, protection of intellectual property and fundamental rights.

The success of smart city initiatives in Bangladesh will therefore depend not only on technological readiness, but also on effective implementation and a comprehensive, future-oriented legal and regulatory framework that ensures transparency, accountability, security, ethical governance and public trust. A resilient governance charter supported by clear legislation, institutional coordination and internationally aligned technical standards would be essential to establishing a secure, interoperable and sustainable smart city ecosystem.

Bangladesh has enacted the Personal Data Protection Act, 2026 (PDPA), and the Cyber Security Act, 2026, which establish the baseline framework for digital governance. The PDPA regulates data collection, processing, storage, transfer and protection, safeguards data subjects’ rights, defines data fiduciaries’ obligations and facilitates conditional cross-border data transfers. The latter protects cyberspace and digital infrastructure by addressing cyber threats and offences, safeguarding critical infrastructure and data, and tackling cybercrimes, including offences involving AI-generated images and digital content.

These legislative developments mark significant progress but appear insufficient to govern the complex legal and technological ecosystem of smart cities. As smart cities thrive on data availability and the increased use of artificial intelligence, open data policies and clear rules on data sharing will encourage innovation by making non-sensitive information accessible to public and private bodies and establishing data usage rights to foster the data economy.

Bangladesh therefore needs comprehensive data governance regulations, data regulations and an artificial intelligence governance policy to support smart city development while safeguarding privacy, cybersecurity, public trust and fundamental rights, and ensuring the responsible and ethical use of AI.

We must remember that smart city infrastructure is vulnerable to cyber threats that can cost us dearly. Therefore, establishing robust cybersecurity standards and measures is essential to ensuring security and interoperability. Beyond an enabling legal framework, a successful smart city ecosystem would also depend on reliable, high-quality and interoperable digital infrastructure.

A recent incident in Bangladesh, in which AI-enabled traffic cameras reportedly misidentified violations, underscores the importance of accurate technology, reliable training datasets and effective system execution. Poorly designed or inadequately tested systems can undermine public trust, lead to erroneous administrative actions and raise legal concerns regarding due process, accountability and liability.

Given the critical importance of smart city projects, Bangladesh should adopt rigorous technical standards and transparent procurement processes, prioritising experienced technology providers and system integrators with proven expertise in large-scale smart city deployments. Established multinational corporations such as Microsoft, Cisco, IBM, Honeywell and Oracle, which have experience in smart city solutions, technical capabilities, compliance standards and a presence in Bangladesh, may be considered.

Nonetheless, engaging renowned technology providers and ensuring independent certification, periodic audits, performance validation and contractual accountability are essential to ensuring secure, accurate, resilient and interoperable smart city infrastructure that supports lawful, reliable and citizen-centric urban governance in Bangladesh.

The writer is a barrister and a technology law practitioner.

title: Bangladesh eyes debut sovereign bond in three months
lead: The government plans to issue a sovereign bond for the first time within the next three months, seeking to diversify its sources of financing, Tanvir Shahriar Ghani, special assistant to the prime minister, said today.
clean_text:
The government plans to issue a sovereign bond for the first time within the next three months, seeking to diversify its sources of financing, Tanvir Shahriar Ghani, special assistant to the prime minister, said today.

He disclosed the plan while speaking to journalists on the sidelines of a two-day international debt conference jointly organised by the finance ministry and the Asian Development Bank (ADB) in Cox’s Bazar.

“We intend to enter the market within the next two to three months,” he said.

Tanvir said the issuance could take place in either New York or London, adding that the size of the bond would be decided later.

Speaking to reporters at the event, Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury stressed the need to diversify Bangladesh’s borrowing sources beyond traditional lenders.

Domestic debt instruments alone would not meet the country’s foreign currency requirements for development projects, he said.

“If we only issue local bonds, we still have to turn to the international market whenever we need foreign currency for development.

“We must move towards alternative financing. Rather than relying solely on multilateral lenders or bilateral sources for loans, we will tap into alternative financing.”

Khosru outlined several financing instruments in the pipeline to mobilise both foreign and domestic capital.

“We are issuing dollar bonds in New York and launching a Bangladesh-dedicated equity fund in Hong Kong,” he said.

“Later, we will also issue Samurai bonds, Panda bonds and local Sukuk bonds.”

title: Parties run on power-centric business model: TIB
lead: Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) has found a serious lack of good governance, transparency, accountability, and democratic practice in the activities of the country’s political parties.
clean_text:
Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) has found a serious lack of good governance, transparency, accountability, and democratic practice in the activities of the country’s political parties.

They also lack internal democratic practices and accountability in political financing, TIB said in its report, “The Institutional Governance of Political Parties in Bangladesh”, launched at its office in Dhaka today.

The study covered 32 parties and reviewed activities from the start of party registration in 2008 through December 2025, using updated data up to August 2026 where relevant.

“The lack of democratic practice, participation and inclusion in party activities has led to the creation of a one-person-centered leadership, familyism, authoritarianism, elitism, majoritarianism and patriarchal culture within the parties,” said the report.

TIB Executive Director Iftekharuzzaman said the exclusion of grassroots members, women, and people from diverse backgrounds allowed dynastic politics and elitism to dominate, depriving capable local leaders of opportunities.

Abuse of power, black money and political criminalisation were fuelling internal conflict and turning political participation or party positions into a “power-centric business model”, he said.

Weak prevention and accountability were normalising the use of money, muscle power and political violence, he added.

TIB found family-centred succession in 10 parties, including the BNP, the Awami League (whose political activities are currently banned), and the Jatiya Party.

The chiefs of 12 parties had served for at least 10 years, seven of them for more than 20. Except for the Communist Party of Bangladesh (CPB), no party constitution limits how many terms an individual can serve as chief.

Although party constitutions provide for leadership elections, most parties choose chiefs by voice vote instead of secret ballot. Only the CPB and Amar Bangladesh Party (AB Party) were found to have had multiple candidates competing for the top position.

National councils were irregular in 16 parties, while decisions often came from individual leaders rather than elected forums. Grassroots committees mainly implemented central decisions, with little say in policy or strategy.

The study said most parties bypassed the Representation of the People Order (RPO) requirement to consider candidate panels proposed by local committees.

Instead, nomination boards interviewed aspirants and gave party chiefs’ preferences the greatest weight.

Many party constitutions lacked clear eligibility criteria. Wealth, muscle power, and unquestioning loyalty influenced selections, particularly in influential parties. TIB reported allegations of awarding nominations in exchange for money in three of these parties.

Businesspeople made up 48.5 percent of candidates and 59.9 percent of elected MPs in the 2026 parliamentary election, according to the study. The corresponding figures in 2024 were 57.6 percent and 65.3 percent.

TIB found a huge difference between the income and expenditure accounts parties officially provided, and the figures estimated in the research.

“In the existing political culture, huge amounts of money are required to conduct the activities of parties; the management of that money is carried out completely through informal and non-transparent processes,” said the report.

TIB estimated that a party maintaining offices and regular activities nationwide down to union ward level could spend Tk 1,532 crore to Tk 2,188 crore annually, excluding election expenses.

By contrast, the highest expenditure reported in the published 2025 accounts of four parties was Tk 23.91 crore, by Jamaat-e-Islami.

The BNP reported Tk 15.26 crore.

The estimate is a model based on organisational reach, not verified spending by any party, so comparing these figures cannot establish undeclared expenditure.

The study said parties lacked clear financial policies and annual budgets.

Local activities were often financed informally by individuals and omitted from central accounts.

None of the 16 active party websites reviewed published financial reports or election expenditure accounts.

TIB also alleged coercive fundraising in some cases, and donations from wealthy people seeking positions, nominations or future benefits.

It further alleged that many parties submitted nominal audit reports prepared for payment, while neither the parties nor the Election Commission published the audited accounts.

Iftekharuzzaman said such personal dependence and financial opacity created a large gap between official accounts and reality.

The study also presented statements from party leaders on election expenditure. One said, “In some areas, Tk 25 lakh is spent in a single day on election expenses.”

Another, referring to election spending, said, “In the election field, the Tk 1,000 note is the smallest denomination.”

A district-level leader said a candidate from a major party spent more than Tk 50 crore in the 12th parliamentary election.

TIB estimated that candidates in the 2026 election spent, on average, 169.5 percent above the permitted limit.

Meeting the organisational requirements for registering a new party could cost Tk 33 lakh to Tk 76 lakh, TIB estimated. This is not a government registration fee but the cost of maintaining the offices and documents the rules require.

TIB said the demanding requirements risked making new entrants dependent on wealthy sponsors, and that irregular payments and political interference in registration had also been alleged.

The constitutions of 18 parties set no minimum ethical standards for membership and no safeguards against people involved in crime obtaining party positions.

Between 18 and 32 percent of candidates in the past five parliamentary elections had faced one or more criminal cases, the study said, though cases alone do not establish guilt.

It also recorded asset increases of more than 50 percent over five years among 67 MPs and the family members of 44 MPs, although asset growth alone does not prove wrongdoing.

TIB found no separate codes of conduct, and no mechanisms for citizens to complain against party activists.

Citing Ain o Salish Kendra data, it reported 4,280 incidents of intra- and inter-party political violence between January 2013 and August 2026, leaving 746 dead and 46,351 injured.

Despite commitments to nominate at least five percent women candidates in the 2026 election, 13 of the studied parties fielded none.

Women made up only 3.1 percent of the nominees of the 12 other participating parties that nominated women, compared with 7.9 percent among independent candidates.

Across the election, women were 83 of 2,028 candidates, or 4.09 percent.

Only two of the 32 parties had women in at least 33 percent of central committee positions, the level parties are required to work towards by 2030.

Jamaat and Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis had none.

TIB said loyalty and family connections often outweighed merit when women were nominated to reserved parliamentary seats.

TIB recommended amending the RPO and party registration rules, publishing independently audited accounts, and empowering the Election Commission to scrutinise finances.

It also recommended holding regular secret-ballot leadership elections, defining tenure limits, expanding women’s and grassroots participation, and introducing effective disciplinary safeguards.

Iftekharuzzaman said internal reforms were essential to ensure good governance within political parties, which he described as key institutions of democracy.

title: Neighbouring country backing attempts to destabilise Bangladesh: Jamaat
lead: Attempts are being made to destabilise parts of the country with the direct backing of a neighbouring country, Leader of the Opposition and Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman said today.
clean_text:
Attempts are being made to destabilise parts of the country with the direct backing of a neighbouring country, Leader of the Opposition and Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman said today.

He made the remarks at a meeting of opposition lawmakers at the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban this afternoon.

Referring to the deteriorating law and order situation, Shafiqur said the government was completely failing to ensure the safety of people's lives and property. If the situation persisted, the country's stability, economy and democratic environment would be seriously affected, he warned.

He also expressed concern over the Matarbari project and the agreement signed with Japan, saying the decisions surrounding the project had created uncertainty among the public. Questions had also arisen over whether the agreement was being used as a cover for a conspiracy to provide a corridor to another country.

He called on the government to clarify its position and make public all the terms of the agreement and related information.

Turning to the garment sector, the country's largest export-earning industry, Shafiqur said it was facing a deep crisis. The government's failure to take effective initiatives to address the sector's problems was posing serious risks to the economy and the labour market, he added.

At the meeting, Opposition Chief Whip and NCP Convener Nahid Islam said the government had failed to play an effective role in preventing the activities and violent actions of what he described as fascist terrorists.

Taking advantage of the government's weakness, various terrorist groups were attempting to create anarchy across the country, he said, adding that covert attacks and violent incidents were taking place in different areas.

Nahid called on all patriotic forces to remain united against fascist terror and subversive activities.

The meeting also discussed several key national issues, including the prime minister's recent visit to Japan, the Matarbari project, renewal of the Ganges water-sharing treaty, alleged irregularities in the appointment of fertiliser dealers, the acceptability of the constitutional amendment committee's activities, and what the opposition described as government negligence in the trial of the July mass killings.

The lawmakers stressed the need for transparent disclosure of all information concerning the Matarbari project's agreement, financing and implementation, as well as matters affecting national interests.

title: Quickly ensure efficient cargo handling at airports: commerce minister
lead: Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir today called for the speedy resolution of infrastructure-related problems to increase cargo-handling capacity at airports and improve the efficiency of international trade by reducing business time and costs.
clean_text:
Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir today called for the speedy resolution of infrastructure-related problems to increase cargo-handling capacity at airports and improve the efficiency of international trade by reducing business time and costs.

The minister made the remarks at a review meeting on increasing airport cargo-handling capacity and the progress of warehouse construction, as part of efforts to boost bilateral trade between Bangladesh and the European Union (EU).

At the meeting, held at the commerce ministry in Dhaka, the minister also said that although issues such as cargo handling and warehouses at airports do not fall directly under the jurisdiction of the commerce ministry, they are closely linked to the country’s trade and export activities.

In particular, modern cargo management at airports is extremely important for expanding trade with the EU, the minister said, adding that the commerce ministry is ready to provide the necessary support to resolve the problems.

Very often, local exporters and importers complain that goods are left unattended outside the cargo villages and warehouses at airports because of a lack of space.

Sometimes, incidents of theft of goods at cargo villages and warehouses take place, as exporters and importers have complained about such incidents.

To expedite the efficient handling of cargo and warehouse operations, the minister proposed establishing an inter-ministerial coordination mechanism, including a representative from the commerce ministry, if necessary.

This would strengthen coordination among all relevant parties and accelerate the implementation of decisions, the minister also said.

Emphasising the need to quickly identify a location and complete the necessary arrangements for a temporary warehouse, Muktadir said that if land needs to be acquired through rental or any other means, a decision must be taken promptly.

The primary objective should be to make the necessary facilities operational as quickly as possible.

The minister also called for the rapid construction of necessary infrastructure to resolve the long-standing cargo-handling problems at the country’s airports.

The customs department is responsible for ensuring the legality of imported and exported goods, required declarations and documentation, and customs-related matters.

Construction and management of warehouses and infrastructure are not the core responsibilities of customs, Muktadir also said.

At the meeting, Minister for Civil Aviation and Tourism Afroza Khanam said concerted efforts are being made to transform Biman Bangladesh Airlines into a safer, more modern and efficient organisation.

She said that resolving long-standing technical and infrastructure-related problems quickly is now a priority.

She emphasised the need to simplify necessary formalities and implement decisions swiftly while ensuring transparency and accountability.

The meeting discussed increasing airport cargo-handling capacity, expediting the clearance of goods, and reducing obstacles to trade and business.

Alongside temporary solutions, progress on the construction of a permanent warehouse was also reviewed.

In this regard, detailed discussions were held on seven potential sites for constructing a temporary warehouse near the airport and four potential sites for a permanent warehouse, according to a statement from the commerce ministry.

title: ১০ হাজার টাকায় ডাকাত দলের কাছে ‘বিক্রি’
lead: নিখোঁজের তিন দিন পর নরসিংদীর রায়পুরার নেসলে কোম্পানির কর্মী শ্যামল চন্দ্র দাসের (৫২) মরদেহ উদ্ধার করেছে পুলিশ। অভিযোগ উঠেছে, ১০ হাজার টাকার বিনিময়ে তাকে ডাকাতদের হাতে তুলে দিয়েছিলেন নৌকার মাঝি। পরে ডাকাতরা তাকে মারধর করে কোম্পানির লক্ষাধিক টাকা ছিনিয়ে নেয়। এমনকি পরিবারের কাছ থেকেও পুলিশের পরিচয়ে ফোন করে ২৫ হাজার টাকা আদায় করে তারা। তারপর হত্যা করে লাশ নদীতে ফেলে দেয়।
clean_text:
নিখোঁজের তিন দিন পর নরসিংদীর রায়পুরার নেসলে কোম্পানির কর্মী শ্যামল চন্দ্র দাসের (৫২) মরদেহ উদ্ধার করেছে পুলিশ। অভিযোগ উঠেছে, ১০ হাজার টাকার বিনিময়ে তাকে ডাকাতদের হাতে তুলে দিয়েছিলেন নৌকার মাঝি। পরে ডাকাতরা তাকে মারধর করে কোম্পানির লক্ষাধিক টাকা ছিনিয়ে নেয়। এমনকি পরিবারের কাছ থেকেও পুলিশের পরিচয়ে ফোন করে ২৫ হাজার টাকা আদায় করে তারা। তারপর হত্যা করে লাশ নদীতে ফেলে দেয়।

রবিবার ব্রাহ্মণবাড়িয়ার নবীনগর উপজেলার সলিমগঞ্জ এলাকা থেকে নদীতে ভাসমান অবস্থায় শ্যামলের মরদেহ উদ্ধার করা হয়। তিনি নরসিংদীর রায়পুরা উপজেলার আমিরগঞ্জ ইউনিয়নের রহিমাবাদ গ্রামের প্রমোদ দাসের ছেলে। শ্যামল নেসলে ডিস্ট্রিবিউশন কোম্পানির কর্মী ছিলেন।

পরিবার ও স্থানীয় সূত্রে জানা যায়, নৌকাযোগে নেসলে কোম্পানির পণ্য আলোকবালি, বটতলী ও চর-আড়ালিয়ার বিভিন্ন দোকানে সরবরাহ করতেন শ্যামল । গত শুক্রবার (৩০ অক্টোবর) প্রতিদিনের মতো আলোকবালিতে পণ্য সরবরাহ করতে যান তিনি। এদিন জহিরুল নামে এক মাঝির নৌকায় করে সেখানে যান। দুপুরে দোকানগুলোতে পণ্য সরবরাহ শেষে বাড়ি ফেরার জন্য একই নৌকায় ওঠেন।

কিন্তু বাড়ি ফেরার পথে মাঝি জহিরুল নির্ধারিত পথ ছেড়ে অন্যদিকে নৌকা চালাতে শুরু করেন। এর কারণ জানতে চাইলে জহিরুল তাকে সহজ ও দ্রুত পথে বাড়ি পৌঁছে দেওয়ার কথা বলেন। একপর্যায়ে নৌকাটি ব্রাহ্মণবাড়িয়ার নবীনগর উপজেলার সলিমগঞ্জের দিকে যেতে থাকে। পরে অন্য একটি নৌকার কাছে গিয়ে শ্যামলকে সেটিতে তুলে দিয়ে বলেন এই নৌকায় উঠলে দ্রুত বাড়ি যেতে পারবেন । শ্যামল তখনো বুঝতে পারেননি যে তাকে ডাকাত দলের কাছে 'বিক্রি' করে দিলেন জহিরুল!

এদিকে, নৌকায় ওঠার পর ডাকাতরা শ্যামলকে বেধড়ক মারধর করে কাছে থাকা কোম্পানির লক্ষাধিক টাকা ছিনিয়ে নেয় । পরে শ্যামলের মোবাইল ফোন থেকে তার পরিবারের সদস্যদের কাছে পুলিশের পরিচয়ে ফোন করা হয়। শ্যামল গুরুতর অসুস্থ বলে জানিয়ে রক্তের প্রয়োজনের কথা বলে দ্রুত ২৫ হাজার টাকা পাঠাতে বলা হয়। পরিবারের সদস্যরা তাদের কথামতো টাকা পাঠান এরপর শ্যামলের মোবাইল ফোনে বারবার যোগাযোগের চেষ্টা করেও কোনো সাড়া পাননি স্বজনেরা। পরে নৌকার মাঝি জহিরুলকে জিজ্ঞাসাবাদ করলে তিনি শ্যামলকে ১০ হাজার টাকার বিনিময়ে অন্য নৌকার মাঝিদের হাতে তুলে দেওয়ার কথা স্বীকার করেন ।

এরপর পরিবারের সদস্যরা রোববার নদীতে মরদেহ ভাসার খবর পান। খবর পেয়ে সলিমগঞ্জ পুলিশ ফাঁড়ির সদস্যরা মরদেহ উদ্ধার করে ময়নাতদন্তের জন্য ব্রাহ্মণবাড়িয়া জেনারেল হাসপাতালের মর্গে পাঠান ময়নাতদন্ত শেষে মরদেহ রায়পুরার গ্রামের বাড়িতে নেওয়া হবে বলে জানিয়েছে পরিবার।

title: সমালোচনার মুখে হ্যান্ডকাফ-বুলেটপ্রুফ জ্যাকেট পরিয়ে ট্রাইব্যুনালে জিয়াউল আহসান
lead: রাজধানীর মতিঝিলের শাপলা চত্বরে হেফাজতে ইসলামের মহাসমাবেশ ঘিরে সংঘটিত গণহত্যার ঘটনায় মানবতাবিরোধী অপরাধের মামলায় গ্রেপ্তার ১১ আসামিকে আন্তর্জাতিক অপরাধ ট্রাইব্যুনালে হাজির করা হয়েছে। সোমবার (১৬ নভেম্বর) সকালে কড়া নিরাপত্তার মধ্য দিয়ে কারাগার থেকে ১০ আসামিকে ট্রাইব্যুনালে আনা হয় এবং বেলা ১২টা ১ মিনিটে হাজির করা হয় সাবেক সেনা কর্মকর্তা মেজর জেনারেল (অব.) জিয়াউল আহসানকে। ট্রাইব্যুনালে আনার সময় জিয়াউল আহসানকে হাতকড়া ও বুলেটপ্রুফ জ্যাকেট পরানো ছিল এবং তার মাথায় হেলমেট দেখা গেছে। এ ছাড়া প্রিজনভ্যান থেকে নামানোর পর সাবেক মন্ত্রী ডা. দীপু মনি, সাংবাদিক ফারজানা রুপা ও শাহরিয়ার কবির ছাড়া বাকি আসামিদের হাত পেছনে নিয়ে হাতকড়া পরানো ছিল। তাদের সবাইকে বুলেটপ্রুফ জ্যাকেট ও মাথায় হেলমেট পরিয়ে ট্রাইব্যুনালের হাজতখানায় নেওয়া হয়। আজ ট্রাইব্যুনাল-২-এর চেয়ারম্যান বিচারপতি নজরুল ইসলাম চৌধুরীর নেতৃত্বাধীন তিন সদস্যের বিচারিক প্যানেলে আসামিপক্ষের শুনানির দিন ধার্য রয়েছে। ক্ষমতাচ্যুত প্রধানমন্ত্রী শেখ হাসিনাসহ এই মামলায় মোট আসামির সংখ্যা ৪১ জন। ট্রাইব্যুনালে হাজির করা অন্য আসামিরা হলেন—জাতীয় সমাজতান্ত্রিক দলের (জাসদ) সভাপতি ও সাবেক তথ্যমন্ত্রী হাসানুল হক ইনু, সাবেক মন্ত্রী ডা. দীপু মনি, তৎকালীন স্বরাষ্ট্র প্রতিমন্ত্রী শামসুল হক টুকু, তৎকালীন খাদ্যমন্ত্রী ড. আবদুর রাজ্জাক, সাবেক মন্ত্রী আবদুল লতিফ সিদ্দিকী, সাবেক পুলিশ মহাপরিদর্শক (আইজিপি) একেএম শহীদুল হক, সাবেক ডিআইজি আবদুল জলিল মণ্ডল, একাত্তরের ঘাতক দালাল নির্মূল কমিটির সভাপতি শাহরিয়ার কবির, ৭১ টিভির সাবেক ব্যবস্থাপনা পরিচালক মোজাম্মেল হক বাবু এবং একই প্রতিষ্ঠানের সাবেক প্রধান প্রতিবেদক ফারজানা রুপা। আদালত প্রাঙ্গণে আনার সময় হাসানুল হক ইনু, আবদুল লতিফ সিদ্দিকীসহ প্রায় সব আসামির মুখেই গাম্ভীর্য দেখা যায়। তবে ব্যতিক্রম ছিলেন সাবেক স্বরাষ্ট্র প্রতিমন্ত্রী শামসুল হক টুকু; তার মুখে স্বাভাবিক হাসি দেখা গেছে। মামলায় প্রসিকিউশনের পক্ষ থেকে মোট দুটি অভিযোগ আনা হয়েছে। প্রথম অভিযোগে ২০১৩ সালের ৫ মে রাজধানীর মতিঝিলের শাপলা চত্বরে ৩২ জনকে হত্যার ঘটনা অন্তর্ভুক্ত করা হয়েছে। আর দ্বিতীয় অভিযোগে পরদিন ৬ মে নারায়ণগঞ্জের সিদ্ধিরগঞ্জে ২০ জনকে হত্যার ঘটনা উল্লেখ করা হয়েছে।
